fullPassage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and (A)[destroy / preserve] digital information for future generations. What has remained (B)[neglected / prioritized] for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are (C)[useless / essential] for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① preserve — neglected — useless: 원문 일치. 디지털 정보를 '보존하는(preserve)' 기준을 만들었지만 장애인의 필요는 '무시되어(neglected)', 자료가 그들에게 '쓸모없게(useless)' 된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② destroy — neglected — useless: (A) destroy(파괴하다)는 preserve(보존하다)와 반대
❌ ③ preserve — prioritized — useless: (B) prioritized(우선시된)는 neglected(무시된)와 반대
❌ ④ preserve — neglected — essential: (C) essential(필수적인)은 useless(쓸모없는)와 반대
det.tip: preserve digital information(보존) / remained neglected(무시) / are useless(쓸모없는)

While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant (B)[progress / failure] in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much (C)[improved / worsened] if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① valuable — failure — improved: (B) failure(실패)는 progress(진전)와 반대
❌ ② worthless — progress — improved: (A) worthless(가치 없는)는 valuable(가치 있는)과 반대
❌ ③ valuable — progress — worsened: (C) worsened(악화된)는 improved(개선된)와 반대
✅ ④ valuable — progress — improved: 원문 일치. 가장 '가치 있는(valuable)' 자료, 전문가의 '진전(progress)', 상황이 '개선될(improved)' 것이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: most valuable resources(가치 있는) / significant progress(진전) / would be much improved(개선)

questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① sighted — distinguishing — embraced: (A) sighted(앞을 보는)는 blind(시각 장애가 있는)와 반대

❌ ④ blind — distinguishing — rejected: (C) rejected(거부한)는 embraced(받아들인)와 반대

det.korean: audience=사용자/관객 (무언가를 읽거나 보거나 사용하는 사람들의 집단)
det.analysis:
❌ ① decade: decade(10년)는 사람 집단이 아닌 기간
✅ ② audience: audience(사용자/관객)는 무언가를 읽거나 보거나 사용하는 사람들의 집단으로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ standard: standard(기준)는 사람 집단이 아님
❌ ④ vision: vision(시력)은 사람 집단이 아님
det.tip: audience = 사용자/관객. keep the largest possible audience in mind가 본문 단서

questions.passage: While professionals __________ (work) in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress, some scholars fail to take these needs into account.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 'professionals __________ in educational technology'에서 명사 professionals를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사가 필요. 전문가들이 '일하는' 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사 working이 적절. work → working
det.tip: 명사 + 현재분사(working) = ~하는 (능동 수식). professionals working = 일하는 전문가들

questions.passage: This situation would be much improved if more projects __________ (embrace) the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 가정법 과거: if절의 동사는 과거형 embraced
det.analysis: 주절에 would be가 쓰인 가정법 과거 문장이므로, if절의 동사는 과거형이 와야 한다. '만약 더 많은 프로젝트가 그 생각을 받아들인다면'이라는 현재 사실의 반대 가정. embrace → embraced
det.tip: 가정법 과거: If + 주어 + 과거동사(embraced), 주어 + would + 동사원형

questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to __________. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: take these needs into account=이러한 필요를 고려하다 — 일부 학자들이 자주 하지 못하는 것
det.analysis:
❌ ① meet every strict deadline(모든 마감을 지키다): 본문의 접근성 요구와 무관
❌ ② reduce the overall costs(비용을 줄이다): 접근성 고려와 무관
❌ ③ finish the projects quickly(프로젝트를 빨리 끝내다): 접근성 고려와 무관
✅ ④ take these needs into account(이러한 필요를 고려하다): 원문 일치. 일부 학자들이 접근성 요구를 '고려하지' 못하는 경우가 많다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: fail to take these needs into account — 요구를 고려하지 못하다

questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep __________ in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the largest possible audience=가능한 가장 많은 사용자 — 디자인 결정 시 염두에 두어야 할 대상
det.analysis:
❌ ① only expert users(전문가 사용자만): 모든 사용자를 포함하라는 논지와 반대
❌ ② the youngest students(가장 어린 학생들): 본문과 무관
✅ ③ the largest possible audience(가능한 가장 많은 사용자): 원문 일치. 디자인 결정 시 '가능한 가장 많은 사용자'를 염두에 두어야 한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ the smallest possible group(가능한 가장 작은 집단): 모든 사용자 포함과 반대
det.tip: keep the largest possible audience in mind — 가장 많은 사용자를 염두에
